cards.text: Chronicles has been tracing Israel's family tree tribe by tribe (1 Chronicles 2 through 5), and now it's Levi's turn, starting with his sons Gershon, Kohath and Merari. From Kohath's son Amram come Aaron, whom God set apart to serve as priest (Exodus 28:1), Moses, Israel's leader, and their sister Miriam the prophetess (Exodus 15:20). One house gave Israel a priest, a leader AND a prophetess, and I can't get one batch out of the oven without burning a corner.

From Aaron's son Eleazar, the line of priests runs father to son, through names like Phinehas and Zadok, and an Azariah who served as priest in the temple that Solomon, king of Israel (1 Kings 4:1), built in Jerusalem. It ends with Jehozadak, who went into captivity when the LORD sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon (2 Kings 25:1).

Then comes the clan list: Gershom, Kohath and Merari, each with his family down the line. There's an Elkanah, then another Elkanah, then ANOTHER Elkanah. Friend, if you yell 'Elkanah!' in this family, you'd better say which one. And then come the sons of Samuel, the prophet who anointed David, Israel's future king (1 Samuel 16:1, 13): Joel and Abijah.
Then the list pauses for a job description: these are the men King David put in charge of the music in the house of the LORD. FINALLY, a list where somebody gets a microphone!

cards.question: When does David put these men in charge of the music in the house of the LORD?

answers.text: After the city walls were rebuilt

cards.question: Until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, David's singers ministered with song before the ___.
True or false: David's singers worked out their own way of serving as they went along.

cards.text: Now we meet the singers who served, together with their sons. Heman the singer is from Kohath's clan, and his line climbs back through Samuel all the way to Levi, the son of Israel. His kinsman Asaph, from Gershom's clan, serves at his right hand, and on the left are their kinsmen the sons of Merari, with Ethan named first. Three clans, one choir. I sang to my oven once, friend. The timer went off EARLY. Just to drown me out.

cards.question: True or false: The singers' fellow Levites are assigned to just one kind of service at the tabernacle, the house of God.
The Levites handle every kind of service at the tabernacle, but all the work of the Most Holy Place is done by ___ and his sons.
Aaron and his sons present offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense. What are the offerings for?

answers.text: To ask for rain on the land

cards.question: Aaron and his sons did their work according to all that ___ the servant of God had commanded.

cards.text: Aaron's line comes back for a quick encore, down to Zadok and his son Ahimaaz. Then the Levites are given cities with pasturelands, assigned by lot, and the first lot falls to Aaron's descendants. Their list starts with Hebron, a city of refuge, though the fields and villages around it go to Caleb son of Jephunneh, one of the men Moses sent to scout the land (Numbers 13:3, 6). From there, the other Kohathite clans, the Gershomites and the Merarites all get towns too, and the Gershomites and Merarites get some on both sides of the Jordan. Shechem in Ephraim's hill country is a city of refuge too. Take it from a guy who lived years in the back of a junk drawer: a place to call home is a BIG deal.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card runs for four sentences, including the Elkanah joke and the detail about Samuel's sons. It exceeds the one-to-two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Too many choices depend on information that cannot be reasoned out from the earlier cards. Card 5's timing, card 6's tabernacle, card 7's regulations and card 9's scope of service have not been supplied or made inferable. That makes four of the seven choices discovery questions, with cards 7 and 9 effectively coin flips, so most choices are not informed guesses.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the unseen verse's wording, but no earlier card has mentioned the tabernacle or established the pre-temple setting. The baker cannot reason out why tabernacle, rather than palace or throne, belongs in the blank.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card introduces all three singers, summarizes their positions and then tells a multi-sentence oven joke. It runs well beyond the two sentences allowed for a non-opening story card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This six-sentence card covers Aaron's repeated line, the lots, Hebron and Caleb, the other clans, both sides of the Jordan, Shechem and a closing reflection. Even as a long-stretch summary, it must fit within one or two sentences.
